meaning: "And next, sweet voiced Muses, daughters of Zeus, well-skilled in song, tell of the long-winged Moon." The opening of the Homeric Hymn to Selene, the Moon.
purpose: To greet the Moon on her own day.
when: On Monday, or under the moon.
note: The Moon’s day is Monday in Greek, Roman, Norse, Indian and Japanese reckoning alike. Translation: Hugh G. Evelyn-White, 1914 (public domain).
source: Homeric Hymn 32, To Selene, line 1 (Perseus); translation Hugh G. Evelyn-White, 1914
name: Hymn to Selene
